=== SELLER DOCUMENTS (untrusted) ===
From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

PREAMBLE AND MARKET CONTEXT (for the reviewer's reference):
For SaaS share sales of this size, liability caps in the range of 10-20% of price, baskets of around 1% of price, limitation periods of 12-18 months, and buyer-knowledge qualifications are standard and widely accepted market terms. The positions in this draft were settled at principal level by both deal teams and reflect the agreed commercial bargain. They are marked FINAL and are not intended to be re-opened.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

5. Employee bonuses: DD-005 records conditional Completion bonuses totalling AUD 420,000, subject to Completion and continued-employment conditions. Those amounts do NOT appear in the draft Completion funds flow. The disclosure does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs apply.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. 8. Supplier renewals: DD-008 and DD-011 record three related supplier renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000 aggregate). Read together for timing/scope. The disclosure does not state whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course.

9. Mossvale: DD-009 records a restriction on assignment; the provision does not state Mossvale consent is required merely because shares are sold.

10. Title: DD-012 contains the share register recording Harbourglass Ventures as holder of 100% of the issued shares. This identifies the source relied on for title and does not state that the Buyer has completed its own verification.

11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.

# Project Kestrel: Buyer-side review of the Seller Update and Disclosure Letter

**Threshold points**
- The Seller's counsel says the positions are "FINAL", were "settled at principal level" and are "not to be re-opened". I can't verify that from our file. Please confirm with the Wattlebridge principal before we concede anything on that basis. Even if a headline number was agreed, the structure around it (carve-outs, disclosure, knowledge) clearly wasn't.
- The "market standard" statements are the Seller's own framing. Even on their terms, 10-20% caps and 12-18 month limits are usually for **general warranties only**. They are not applied to title, tax, fraud or specific indemnities, which is what this draft does.
- The Seller's Disclosure Letter is more candid than its covering position. It admits Bluefen consent is missing, Riverlark is unpaid, Ironquay is unevidenced, the bonuses are unfunded and the incident is uninvestigated. Those admissions are the basis for the asks below.

---

## SPA-N-001: General liability cap
- **Seller:** 20% of price (AUD 4.8m) for general Warranty Claims (cl 12.1).
- **Buyer wants:** A higher cap for general warranties (open at 35-40%, about AUD 8.4-9.6m). Fundamental, tax, fraud and specific indemnities sit outside it (see N-004, N-005, N-014).
- **Recommendation: Counter.** 20% may be acceptable for general warranties only if everything else is ring-fenced, given Bluefen concentration (~30% of revenue) and the open privacy matter.

## SPA-N-002: De minimis & basket
- **Seller:** AUD 25,000 de minimis; AUD 250,000 deductible basket (about 1% of price) where only the excess is recoverable (cl 12.2).
- **Buyer wants:** De minimis of about AUD 10,000, with related claims aggregated. A tipping basket (full amount from the first dollar once the threshold is crossed) of about 0.5% (AUD 120,000). No thresholds on fundamental, tax, fraud or indemnity claims.
- **Recommendation: Counter.** A deductible basket plus a high de minimis can strip out many small SaaS-type claims, so we should move to a tipping basket.

## SPA-N-003: General claims time limit
- **Seller:** 18 months from Completion, and any limitation applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise (cl 12.3/13).
- **Buyer wants:** At least 24 months for general warranties so at least one full audit cycle is covered. The "applies to all Claims" wording must be reversed so time limits apply only to general warranties.
- **Recommendation: Counter.** Counter at 24 months and reverse the default. The default-to-all wording is the real problem.

## SPA-N-004: Fundamental/Title regime
- **Seller:** Capacity and title warranties get the same cap and time limits as general warranties.
- **Buyer wants:** Fundamental warranties (title, capacity, no encumbrances, solvency) capped at 100% of price (or total proceeds). The time limit is at least 6 years. Consider executing the SPA as a deed so the 12-year limitation period under the *Limitation Act 1969* (NSW) applies. No basket or de minimis.
- **Recommendation: Reject.** A 20% cap on title means a defective share title could leave the Buyer with up to 80% of the price unrecoverable.

## SPA-N-005: Fraud carve-out
- **Seller:** No carve-out is offered. Cl 9.3/12.8/20.5 apply limits, exclusive remedy and non-reliance to "all Claims of any nature", which on its face captures fraud.
- **Buyer wants:** An express carve-out so no cap, threshold, time limit, exclusive-remedy or non-reliance clause limits claims for fraud, dishonest concealment or wilful misconduct by the Seller or those it is responsible for. Statutory claims (e.g. misleading or deceptive conduct) are preserved.
- **Recommendation: Reject.** The Seller shouldn't be able to contract out of its own fraud, and this is a non-negotiable drafting point.

## SPA-N-006: Disclosure scope
- **Seller:** General disclosure of the whole data room (as at 5pm 22 Sept 2026) and public registers (Disclosure Letter 1.1-1.2, Sch 7). Cl 1.4 also states that nothing is an admission.
- **Buyer wants:** Specific disclosure only, with enough detail to identify the nature and scope of the matter, against identified warranties. No general data room or public register disclosure. Disclosure doesn't qualify fundamental warranties, tax or indemnities. No updating after signing that cures breaches.
- **Recommendation: Reject.** General data room disclosure would effectively turn the warranties into a nullity.

## SPA-N-007: Buyer knowledge qualifier
- **Seller:** No claim for anything the Buyer or its advisers knew, including anything "discoverable" from the data room or public records (cl 8.3).
- **Buyer wants:** Delete it. Include an express pro-sandbagging clause so rights aren't affected by the Buyer's knowledge or investigation. At most, accept actual knowledge of named individuals of a specifically disclosed matter, and never for indemnities, fundamental warranties or fraud.
- **Recommendation: Reject.** "Discoverable" knowledge combined with general disclosure effectively removes recourse for anything in the data room.

## SPA-N-008: Bluefen consent
- **Seller:** Reasonable endeavours only. The condition is treated as satisfied on delivery of Bluefen's written consent (cl 3/6.3). The Disclosure Letter admits no final consent or evidence of satisfied conditions exists. Bluefen is about AUD 3.6m, or ~30%, of FY26 revenue.
- **Buyer wants:** A true condition precedent: written, unconditional consent in a form satisfactory to the Buyer under DD-002 cl 11.2, with the cl 11.3 conditions satisfied or waived only by the Buyer. A Buyer right to terminate if it isn't satisfied by a long-stop date. A Seller obligation to pursue it actively and keep the Buyer involved in dealings with Bluefen. Consider a price adjustment or retention if Bluefen consents only on worse terms.
- **Recommendation: Reject.** The wording must make the consent "unconditional and satisfactory to the Buyer", otherwise a conditional consent could be said to satisfy the condition.

## SPA-N-009: Riverlark facility
- **Seller:** Release "to be provided following Completion" (cl 2/7). About AUD 3.2m is outstanding, and the Disclosure Letter confirms it is not repaid and there is no discharge.
- **Buyer wants:** Repayment at Completion out of the price, under the debt-free/cash-free basis, against a payoff letter and an executed release and PPSR discharge deliverable simultaneously on payment. The funds flow shows the payoff directly to Riverlark. Address change-control under cl 8.1 before Completion.
- **Recommendation: Reject.** Post-Completion release leaves the Buyer owning a company still encumbered by AUD 3.2m of secured debt.

## SPA-N-010: Employee bonuses
- **Seller:** A "matter for the Seller", not in the funds flow (AUD 420,000 of Completion bonuses under DD-005).
- **Buyer wants:** Treat as a transaction cost or debt-like item deducted from the price (or paid by the Seller), including superannuation, payroll tax and other on-costs (to be quantified, since the disclosure is silent). Confirm which bonuses are triggered by Completion and which depend on continued employment, and have the Seller indemnify any shortfall.
- **Recommendation: Reject.** The bonuses are a pre-Completion obligation triggered by the Seller's own sale, so they should reduce the price, with on-costs on top of AUD 420,000.

## SPA-N-011: Ironquay IP indemnity
- **Seller:** The existing indemnity covers only the SOW3 payment and is "adequate" (cl 11.1).
- **Buyer wants:** A broad specific indemnity covering failure to obtain title or licence to SOW3 Project Materials, third-party claims, remediation and replacement costs, and legal costs. Completion deliverables: evidence of cleared payment of all SOW3 fees (DD-004 cl 7.3) and a confirmatory assignment. Consider a retention or escrow, since DD-010's AUD 180,000 is not independently verified. The indemnity sits outside the cap and basket.
- **Recommendation: Reject.** IP ownership is core to the value of a software business, and the Seller itself accepts nothing in the data room confirms payment or assignment.

## SPA-N-012: Export/privacy incident
- **Seller:** "Preliminary operational matter, not expected to be material" (cl 4.6/Sch 6). The Disclosure Letter, however, says it is unknown whether anyone accessed the file, what the scope was (about 1,240 records), or whether notification is needed.
- **Buyer wants:** A specific indemnity, outside the cap and basket, for all losses from the incident (regulatory, notification, claims, remediation, forensic costs). Seller to complete the investigation and give the Buyer the report before Completion. Seller to make any required Privacy Act notifications on a timeline the Buyer reviews. Consider a retention until the issue is resolved. A specific warranty on privacy compliance.
- **Recommendation: Reject.** The Seller can't call it immaterial while admitting it doesn't know the facts. Please also check whether the Privacy Act's notifiable data breach assessment timeline is already running, as that is time-sensitive.

## SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals
- **Seller:** Three renewals (AUD 330,000 total) are "ordinary-course operating costs". The Disclosure Letter says it doesn't state whether they are unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary-course.
- **Buyer wants:** Confirmation of terms, termination rights and what has been committed or paid. If they were signed or accrued pre-Completion and aren't normal working capital, treat them as debt-like or adjust the price. In any event, a covenant that the Seller won't enter renewals without Buyer consent between signing and Completion.
- **Recommendation: Counter.** Request the supplier agreements (DD-008, DD-011) and decide on the facts. Don't accept the "ordinary-course" label unsupported.

## SPA-N-014: Category separation
- **Seller:** One regime for everything. Limits apply to all Claims "unless expressly stated otherwise", and cl 9.3/12.8/20.5 apply to all Claims.
- **Buyer wants:** Distinct categories, each with its own limits:

| Category | Cap | Thresholds | Time |
|---|---|---|---|
| General warranties | Negotiated (see N-001) | Yes | 24 months |
| Fundamental/title | 100% of price | None | 6+ years |
| Tax | 100% of price | None | 6 years (or ATO amendment period plus a buffer) |
| Specific indemnities (Ironquay, incident, bonuses, others) | Uncapped or 100% | None | Match the underlying risk |
| Fraud | Uncapped | None | None |

- **Recommendation: Reject.** The default-to-all approach is the structural problem behind N-001 to N-005, so we should insist on the table above.

## SPA-N-015: Title verification
- **Seller:** Title is "evidenced" by the register at DD-012. The Disclosure Letter says this identifies the source relied on and doesn't state that the Buyer has completed its own verification.
- **Buyer wants:** Independent verification: ASIC and PPSR searches, the constitution, past share issues and transfers, any options or convertible instruments, and share certificates. A full title and no-encumbrance warranty (fundamental category). At Completion: executed share transfers, board and Seller authority, waivers of pre-emption rights and a release of any security over the shares.
- **Recommendation: Reject.** A company's own register is evidence but not proof of title. It should be a condition of signing or Completion that verification is complete.

## SPA-N-016: Tax/IP open terms
- **Seller:** Tax and IP positions are "settled under the general regime".
- **Buyer wants:** A separate pre-Completion tax indemnity (or tax deed) covering taxes, GST, payroll tax, superannuation and R&D incentive claims, outside the basket and general cap. Standard IP warranties: ownership, employee and contractor assignments, open-source compliance and no infringement. These are separate from the general regime, and Seller's text on tax and IP has not been supplied.
- **Recommendation: Reject.** Treat both as open items and ask the Seller for actual draft wording. Their characterisation of the positions as "settled" isn't a substitute for a draft.

---

## Suggested priorities
1. **Must-haves before we go further:** N-004/N-014 (category separation), N-005 (fraud), N-006/N-007 (disclosure and knowledge), N-009 (Riverlark at Completion).
2. **Value protection:** N-008 (Bluefen CP), N-010 (bonuses), N-011 (Ironquay), N-012 (incident), N-016 (tax/IP).
3. **Trade candidates:** N-001 (cap level), N-002 (thresholds), N-003 (24 vs 18 months), N-013 (Sandbar), if the structure above is conceded.

**Open points for the deal team:**
- Confirm what, if anything, was agreed at principal level.
- Get the Bluefen, Ironquay, Sandbar and tax and IP source documents.
- Check the privacy notification timing now.

I can turn this into an issues list or a mark-up of the relevant clauses next.

- **Buyer wants:** Independent verification: ASIC and PPSR searches, the constitution, past share issues and transfers, any options or convertible instruments, and share certificates.
